events.title: Philistines Arrival
events.description: Philistines migrated from Aegean region to eastern Mediterranean coast, settling in Gaza Strip coastal area today. They established five city-states (Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron, Gath), frequently conflicting with Israelites. The name 'Palestine' derives from 'Philistia'.

events.title: Israel-Judah Kingdom Period
events.description: Hebrews under David and Solomon established unified Kingdom of Israel, capital Jerusalem. After kingdom split, northern Israel Kingdom and southern Judah Kingdom competed with Philistines, Assyria and Babylon for this land.

events.title: Babylonian Conquest and Exile
events.description: Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and First Temple, Jewish elite exiled. 538 BCE Persia allowed Jews to return and rebuild temple. This land changed hands repeatedly under Persian, Hellenistic and Roman rule.

events.title: Rome Destroys Second Temple
events.description: Rome suppressed Jewish revolt, General Titus besieged Jerusalem, destroyed Second Temple. After Bar Kokhba revolt 135 CE, Rome renamed Judea 'Syria Palaestina', attempting to erase Jewish connection. Many Jews dispersed, but communities remained in Galilee and elsewhere.

events.title: Arab Muslim Conquest
events.description: Arab Muslims defeated Byzantines at Battle of Yarmouk, conquered Palestine. Palestine gradually Arabized and Islamized, but Christian and Jewish communities continued. Jerusalem became Islam's third holiest site (Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa Mosque).

events.title: Crusader Kingdom
events.description: Crusaders conquered Jerusalem, established Kingdom of Jerusalem. Crusaders massacred Muslims and Jews. 1187 Saladin recaptured Jerusalem. Crusaders retained coastal strongholds until 1291 when expelled by Mamluks.

events.title: Ottoman Rule Begins
events.description: Ottoman Empire conquered Palestine, ruling 400 years until WWI. Ottoman rule relatively tolerant of religious diversity. Palestine divided into several administrative districts. Population mainly Arab Muslims and Christians, plus small Jewish communities.

events.title: Palestine Before Zionism
events.description: Late 19th century, Palestine population about 500,000, 90% Arab (Muslims and Christians), 10% Jews (mainly in religious cities like Jerusalem, Safed). Economy mainly agricultural, society organized by villages and clans. Palestinian identity began forming.

events.title: Publication of 'The Jewish State'
events.description: Theodor Herzl published 'The Jewish State', marking beginning of modern Zionist movement. Herzl advocated establishing independent Jewish state as solution to European antisemitism. First Zionist Congress held in Basel in 1897.

events.title: Jewish Immigration Wave Begins
events.description: Driven by European antisemitism and Zionism, Jews began mass immigration to Palestine (Aliyah). First Aliyah (1882-1903) about 30,000, Second (1904-1914) about 40,000. Jews established collective farms (kibbutzim) and new cities like Tel Aviv, purchasing land.

events.title: Balfour Declaration
events.description: British Foreign Secretary Balfour declared support for establishing 'Jewish national home' in Palestine. This commitment ignored local 90% Arab population. Palestinian Arabs felt betrayed, feared replacement. Declaration sowed seeds of Jewish-Arab conflict.

events.title: British Mandate
events.description: League of Nations granted Britain Palestine mandate. Britain attempted to balance Zionism and Arab nationalism, but both increasingly conflicted. Jewish immigration continued increasing (especially 1930s fleeing Nazis), land purchases intensified tensions.

events.title: Western Wall Riots
events.description: Conflict between Jews and Muslims over religious rights at Jerusalem Western Wall (Wailing Wall)/Al-Buraq Wall triggered massive riots. Massacres occurred against Jews in Hebron and Safed, about 133 Jews and 116 Arabs killed.

events.title: Nazi-Era Jewish Immigration Wave
events.description: After Nazis came to power in Germany, hundreds of thousands of Jews fled Europe to Palestine. Jewish population increased from about 170,000 to about 450,000. Mass immigration intensified Arab panic and anger, leading to 1936 Great Revolt.

events.title: Arab Great Revolt
events.description: Palestinian Arabs launched massive uprising against British rule, Jewish immigration and land purchases. Revolt included general strikes, boycotts and armed struggle. Britain brutally suppressed, destroying villages, executing leaders. Revolt weakened Palestinian Arab leadership, laying foundation for 1948 catastrophe.

events.title: UN Partition Resolution
events.description: UN General Assembly voted for Resolution 181, dividing Palestine into Jewish state (56% territory, though Jews only 33% population) and Arab state (43%), Jerusalem internationalized (1%). Jews accepted but Arabs rejected as unjust. Civil war erupted after resolution.

events.title: Civil War and Village Destruction
events.description: After partition resolution, Palestinian Jewish and Arab communities erupted in civil war. Jewish armed organizations (Haganah, Irgun, Lehi) executed plans, occupying strategic points, destroying Arab villages. Deir Yassin village massacre (April 1948) killed 100+ civilians, causing panic. Arabs began fleeing.

events.title: Israel's Establishment and Nakba
events.description: Israel declared independence, Arab states invaded. In war, about 750,000 Palestinians (over half total population) fled or were expelled, becoming refugees. Over 400 Palestinian villages destroyed or renamed. Palestinians call it 'Nakba' (catastrophe). Palestinian society completely collapsed, dispersed everywhere.

events.title: Division: West Bank, Gaza, Israel
events.description: After war Palestine divided into three parts: Israel controlled 78% original Palestine (including most coast and Galilee), Jordan annexed West Bank and East Jerusalem, Egypt administered Gaza Strip. About 150,000 Palestinians remained in Israel, becoming second-class citizens. Refugees scattered in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria and Gaza refugee camps.

events.title: PLO Established
events.description: With Arab League support, Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) established, goal to liberate Palestine. 1969 Arafat became chairman. PLO engaged in armed struggle and terrorism, also diplomatic efforts for international recognition.

events.title: Six-Day War and Occupation
events.description: Israel in Six-Day War occupied West Bank, Gaza Strip, East Jerusalem, Golan Heights and Sinai Peninsula. All Palestine fell under Israeli control. UN Resolution 242 required Israel withdraw from occupied territories, Israel began establishing settlements.

events.title: Fatah's First Operation
events.description: Fatah, led by Yasser Arafat, launched its first armed operation against Israel, marking the beginning of Palestinian armed resistance movement.

events.title: PLO Gains International Recognition
events.description: Arab League recognized PLO as sole legitimate representative of Palestinian people. Arafat addressed UN, saying 'one hand holds olive branch, other freedom fighter's gun'. PLO gained observer status, international recognition increased.

events.title: Black September
events.description: Jordan's King Hussein expelled PLO from Jordan after conflict, killing thousands. PLO moved to Lebanon, event named Black September.

events.title: Munich Olympics Attack
events.description: Black September Organization attacked Israeli athletes at Munich Olympics, killing 11. Event shocked world and highlighted Palestinian cause.

events.title: First Intifada
events.description: Palestinians in occupied territories launched massive uprising (Intifada, meaning 'shaking off'), using stones, strikes and civil disobedience against Israeli occupation. Israel violently suppressed, bone-breaking policy drew international criticism. Hamas (Islamic Resistance Movement) formed during this period, challenging PLO leadership.

events.title: Israel Invades Lebanon
events.description: Israel invaded Lebanon to expel PLO. Sabra and Shatila massacre occurred, thousands of Palestinian refugees killed.

events.title: State of Palestine Declared
events.description: PLO in Algiers declared State of Palestine independent, territory 1967 borders (West Bank and Gaza). Over 100 countries recognized, but Israel and US refused. This marked PLO shift from liberating all Palestine to two-state solution.

events.title: Oslo Accords
events.description: Rabin and Arafat signed Oslo Accords at White House. Israel recognized PLO, PLO recognized Israel and renounced violence. Agreement established Palestinian Authority (PA), gradually taking over parts of West Bank and Gaza. Final status issues (borders, Jerusalem, refugees, settlements) left for negotiation. Oslo brought hope for peace.

events.title: Palestinian Authority Established
events.description: Arafat returned to Gaza, Palestinian Authority began operating, controlling Gaza and parts of West Bank (Area A). But Israel retained control of most West Bank, borders, water resources. Settlements continued expanding, causing Palestinian dissatisfaction.

events.title: Rabin Assassinated
events.description: Israeli PM Rabin assassinated by far-right Jew, peace process lost key driver. Successors Peres and Netanyahu weakened Oslo commitments. Settlements accelerated expansion, negotiations stalled.

events.title: Camp David Summit Failed
events.description: Clinton convened Barak and Arafat for final status negotiations. Though close, failed to reach agreement on Jerusalem status, borders and refugee right of return. Both sides blamed each other. After summit failure, Second Intifada erupted.

events.title: Second Intifada
events.description: Sharon's visit to Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif triggered Palestinian uprising, more violent than first. Hamas and Islamic Jihad launched suicide bombings, killing hundreds of Israeli civilians. Israeli military operations, targeted killings, curfews and closures killed thousands of Palestinians. Violence destroyed peace hopes, both societies deeply traumatized.

events.title: Arab Peace Initiative and Separation Wall
events.description: Saudi proposed Arab Peace Initiative: Israel withdraw to 1967 borders, in exchange for peace with all Arab states. Israel didn't respond. Israel began building separation barrier in West Bank, deeply annexing land, dividing Palestinian communities. International Court of Justice ruled it illegal.

events.title: Arafat Dies
events.description: Arafat died in Paris, cause of death mysterious (possibly poisoning). He was symbol of Palestinian national movement, but also criticized for corruption and authoritarianism. Abbas succeeded as PLO and Palestinian Authority chairman.

events.title: Israel Withdraws from Gaza
events.description: Sharon unilaterally withdrew all settlements and military from Gaza. But Israel retained control of borders, airspace and sea. Withdrawal didn't bring peace, instead led to Hamas takeover.

events.title: Hamas Wins Election
events.description: Hamas defeated Fatah in Palestinian Legislative Council elections, winning majority seats. West and Israel refused to recognize Hamas government, imposed sanctions. Fatah-Hamas power struggle evolved into violence.

events.title: Palestine Gains UN Observer State Status
events.description: UN General Assembly voted to upgrade Palestine to non-member observer state status. 138 countries voted in favor, 9 against (including US and Israel). This was major diplomatic victory for Palestinians.

events.title: Palestinian Division
events.description: Hamas controlled Gaza Strip after brief civil war. Fatah controlled West Bank. Palestine split into two governments, reconciliation efforts repeatedly failed. Division severely weakened Palestinian negotiating position.

events.title: Gaza Blockade
events.description: Israel imposed tight blockade on Hamas-controlled Gaza, controlling borders, airspace and sea, restricting movement of people and goods. Egypt mostly closed Rafah crossing. Blockade caused humanitarian disaster, economic collapse, unemployment rate up to 50%, electricity and water shortages. 2 million people trapped in 'open-air prison'.

events.title: Operation Cast Lead
events.description: Israel launched large-scale military operation in Gaza, killing about 1,400 Palestinians (mostly civilians). International community condemned disproportionate use of force. Gaza suffered massive destruction.

events.title: Gaza Wars
events.description: Israel and Hamas had multiple military conflicts. 2014 'Protective Edge' operation bloodiest, lasting 50 days, 2200+ Palestinians and 73 Israelis killed. Gaza suffered massive destruction, thousands of homes destroyed. Each conflict cycle of rockets and airstrikes, but failed to resolve fundamental issues.

events.title: Trump Recognizes Jerusalem as Israel Capital
events.description: Trump recognized Jerusalem as Israel capital, moved US embassy to Jerusalem. This broke international consensus (Jerusalem status should be resolved through negotiations), angered Palestinians, triggered protests and violence.

events.title: Abraham Accords
events.description: UAE, Bahrain and other countries normalized relations with Israel, bypassing Palestinian issue. Arab states no longer made Palestine precondition for relations with Israel. Palestinians felt abandoned and betrayed, negotiating leverage weakened.

events.title: Jerusalem Tensions and Gaza Conflict
events.description: Eviction of Palestinian families in Jerusalem Sheikh Jarrah neighborhood and police raid on Al-Aqsa Mosque triggered massive protests. Hamas fired rockets at Israel, Israel heavily bombarded Gaza. 11-day conflict caused 250+ Palestinian and 13 Israeli deaths.

events.title: Hamas Attack and Israel-Hamas War
events.description: Hamas launched unprecedented massive raid from Gaza, killing about 1200 Israelis, kidnapping about 250 hostages. Israel launched massive military operation in Gaza, vowing to destroy Hamas. War caused tens of thousands of Palestinian deaths in Gaza (mostly civilians), 2.3 million displaced, 80% buildings damaged.

events.title: Gaza Destruction and Humanitarian Catastrophe
events.description: Israeli bombing and ground operations turned Gaza into rubble. Hospitals, schools, mosques destroyed. Famine threatened, disease spread, basic services collapsed. UN and human rights organizations warned of genocide risk. International Court of Justice and International Criminal Court intervened to investigate. World divided: West supported Israel's self-defense right but criticized civilian casualties; Global South and Arab world condemned Israel. Massive protests demanded ceasefire.

events.title: Hopeless Future
events.description: Palestinians endured 76 years of catastrophe, still no state. West Bank fragmented by settlements (700,000 settlers), daily violence and restrictions. Gaza is hell on earth, facing impossible reconstruction task after war. Jerusalem gradually Judaized. Refugees (6 million) still in camps, return hopeless. Two-state solution dead, one-state means apartheid. Young Palestinian generation loses peace hope, radicalization grows. International community failed to resolve conflict, US biased toward Israel. Palestine divided, leadership aging and corrupt. But Palestinians persist with 'sumud' (steadfastness), maintaining identity through culture, art and resistance. Their fate entangled with Israel's, peace and justice remain distant dream. Palestine question one of 20th century's most enduring unresolved conflicts, its resolution crucial for Middle East and world peace.
